parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, is an inert gas that makes up 78% of the Earth's atmosphere.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: Draw a 'dot-and-cross' diagram of a nitrogen molecule. Show outer electrons only.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Nitrogen, $\text{N}_2$, and oxygen, $\text{O}_2$, react together in the air during lightning strikes to form nitrogen monoxide, $\text{NO}$.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Explain why the reaction of $\text{N}_2$ and $\text{O}_2$ occurs during lightning strikes.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write two equations to suggest how the NO formed reacts further to create nitric acid, $\text{HNO}_3$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Nitrate fertilisers are used to provide nitrogen for plant growth. Uncontrolled use of these can cause a reduction in animal and plant life in natural water supplies.

Explain how uncontrolled use of nitrate fertilisers can cause this problem.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Some soils have compounds such as ammonium nitrate, calcium carbonate and calcium hydroxide added to them.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: Suggest why calcium hydroxide is added to some soils.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
When calcium hydroxide reacts with compounds containing the ammonium ion, $\text{NH}_4^+$, a gas is produced.

State the identity of this gas and explain why the reaction occurs.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
Another fertiliser, calcium ammonium nitrate, is formed when solid calcium carbonate is added to a mixture of aqueous ammonium nitrate and dilute nitric acid.

Suggest what would be observed in this reaction.

parts.label: (d)(iv)
parts.text:
Calcium nitrate decomposes at a higher temperature than calcium ammonium nitrate.

Write an equation for the thermal decomposition of calcium nitrate.
